     6  module
     7  
     8  public import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.TypeTags.Finite
     9  public import Mathlib.Algebra.MonoidAlgebra.Basic
    10  public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.VectorSpace
    11  public import Mathlib.RingTheory.SimpleModule.Basic
    12  public import Mathlib.RepresentationTheory.Semisimple
    13  
    14  /-!
    15  # Maschke's theorem
    16  
    17  We prove **Maschke's theorem** for finite groups,
    18  in the formulation that every submodule of a `k[G]` module has a complement,
    19  when `k` is a field with `Fintype.card G` invertible in `k`.
    20  
    21  We do the core computation in greater generality.
    22  For any commutative ring `k` in which `Fintype.card G` is invertible,
    23  and a `k[G]`-linear map `i : V → W` which admits a `k`-linear retraction `π`,
    24  we produce a `k[G]`-linear retraction by
    25  taking the average over `G` of the conjugates of `π`.
    26  
    27  ## Implementation Notes
    28  
    29  * These results assume `IsUnit (Fintype.card G : k)` which is equivalent to the more
    30    familiar `¬(ringChar k ∣ Fintype.card G)`.
    31  
    32  ## Future work
    33  It's not so far to give the usual statement, that every finite-dimensional representation
    34  of a finite group is semisimple (i.e. a direct sum of irreducibles).
    35  -/
    36  
    37  @[expose] public section
    38  
    39  noncomputable section
    40  
"}]
